events.text: Request filed and logged by the City.
City sent a cost estimate of $108 and asked for a $54 deposit.

ETLC asked the City for an exhibit missing from the released 2009 water system purchase contract, plus related records on the contract's water supply terms, and asked that anything outside this request be treated as a new request.

requests.waiting: The Attorney General's ruling on the withheld records, due by about mid-December 2026, and the rest of the City's release.
found: The City released a first batch of records on Oct. 29. ETLC is reviewing them and will post them here.

requests.asked: Well permit applications for Amp Z, Verdant Industries or anyone seeking groundwater at the former Southland Paper Mill site; correspondence with those companies since 2024; any well application in Angelina County since 2024 for more than 25,000 gallons a day; and board agendas and minutes discussing them.

events.text: Request filed.

The District answered in writing: no well applications near the Southland mill site in the past two years and no contact with Amp Z or Verdant. It disclosed that WattBridge was approved in late 2024 and early 2025 for wells totaling 80 million gallons a year for a power plant in the north of the county, never drilled, and in March 2026 asked for 1.5 billion gallons a year for a 24/7 plant; that request has been on hold since July 2026 at the company's request. The District asked whether ETLC still wanted the documents and requested until Oct. 16 to gather them.
ETLC confirmed it still wants the WattBridge permit applications and the related board agendas and minutes, and dropped the rig supply well applications.

The District sent board agendas and minutes from Aug. 5, 2024 (Angelina WSC) and Feb. 10, 2025 (WattBridge). It said WattBridge never drilled its two approved wells, so no permits were issued, and that the later 1.5-billion-gallon request came mostly by phone with no board meeting or public hearing. The District expects to send the rest by Nov. 9.

The District said it will try to finish all of ETLC's requests by Nov. 9 and asked for one list of the records still needed. ETLC sent it the same day: the WattBridge applications and any records of its 1.5-billion-gallon request, and the Hudson Water Supply well records.

requests.waiting: The rest of the records, including information on the Hudson well. The District expects to send them by Nov. 9.

clock.start_note: ETLC confirmed which records it still wants

found: No one has applied to drill wells near the old Southland mill in the past two years, and the District says it has had no contact with Amp Z or Verdant Industries.

On Feb. 10, 2025, the District's board approved WattBridge's application for two wells, totaling 80 million gallons a year, for a power plant in the north of the county. The wells were never drilled, and the District says no permits were ever issued.
At that vote, board member Roger Russell abstained. The minutes say he is the driller.

In March or early April 2026, WattBridge asked, mostly by phone, for 1.5 billion gallons a year. There was no board meeting or public hearing on it. The District told the company to resubmit under rules adopted March 23, 2026. The company put the project on hold in July, and the District now considers it dead until updated information arrives.

On Aug. 5, 2024, the board approved a new Angelina WSC well on Schoolcraft Road off FM 326 for 75 million gallons a year and raised the permitted amounts for three existing wells, which were at 80% of their limits. No one spoke at the public hearing.
